items.caption:
🎪
Nobody tells you self care can be lonely AF.

I think most people lose themselves in relationships, family, kids, work, community… just being close to people. Eating together, relaxing, watching dumb shows, passing time with people you love.

But taking care of your body? That’s weirdly isolating.

Early mornings. Time in the sauna. Group fitness where somehow you still feel completely alone. Yoga where looking someone in the face feels socially incorrect.

So I don’t know… why is self care so lonely. Is it just me?

Is it because my person isn’t with me every moment of the day? too awkward to make gym friends? 

is my body trying to teach me it’s OK to be alone and focus on myself for a while?

No idea.

Sometimes it feels powerful. Sometimes it sucks.

At least I look good.

Turns out finding your people sometimes looks like getting thrown on a boat and being told to pull a rope.

items.caption:
🎪
I made myself a promise:

To intentionally become a male model by 50.

I’m 48 today.

The role of a “model” means a lot of different things.

This carousel is a glimpse into the notes I’ve been collecting and shaping throughout that journey. These generated slides represent what being a model means to me.

It’s not a rulebook.

It’s simply the framework that’s helped me become more intentional with my body, style, storytelling, presence, and the character I’m becoming.

The biggest lesson?

Modeling isn’t just about standing in front of a camera.

It’s about becoming someone worth remembering.

None of this happened alone. I’m incredibly grateful for every mentor, photographer, designer, coach, agency, friend, and company that’s invested in me along the way. You know who you are.

I hope something in here inspires you to intentionally model the life you want to live.

Undeniably a model.

Much of my creativity comes from loneliness. 

Or, for that matter, forcing myself to be alone, comforting myself, crying alone, looking at photos and videos of my life, wishing things were different, but loving exactly what they are.

Being broken isn’t meant to be private. Healing is a competitive sport just as much as it is a solo adventure.

But know that none of us will ever be healed. Enough.

Only broken. 
Together.

items.caption:
Every time I’ve stepped into something that felt way outside my comfort zone… something I never saw myself doing… the game changer wasn’t confidence.

It was proximity.

Find someone who’s already done the thing.

Not to copy them—but to learn how they think, how they move, how they handle the moments you haven’t faced yet.

Support their work.

Be genuinely in their corner.

And don’t be afraid to share your messy, in-progress journey with them.

Because something powerful happens when you do…

You stop comparing… and start connecting.
You stop performing… and start growing.

And before you even realize it, you’re surrounded by people who are ACTUALLY rooting for you.

That’s the real magic.

That’s the symbiotic dance of teacher and student.

Grateful for the mentors in my life… 

@lord_proverbs_illmaticscream @j.m.syron and @aquariusfunkk being a very special influences this season.

honestly, they’ve been the spice in everything I’m becoming 🌶️❤️‍🔥🤍🖤

items.caption:
2017 → 2020 Throwback Thursday

Back then I was somewhere around 360–370 lbs.
Today I stepped on the scale and saw 235.

I feel stronger, clearer, and healthier than I have in years… but looking at these photos reminds me something important: these were still beautiful, happy times.

One photo is a tumbledown mountain adventure with my daughter.

Now she’s out exploring the wilderness of Tacoma and the world living the kinds of adventures she could only dream about back then.

The other photo was taken at Mechanics Hall surrounded by creators and community.

Funny thing—I noticed that painting behind us isn’t even on that wall anymore. Time moves, spaces change, people evolve.

But the moments?
Those stay.

Grateful for every version of myself that got me here.

items.caption:
Proud Model Momma Moment ✨

People often tell me I’m unapproachable. Intense.
In big public rooms, that can make it hard to connect.

So I practice the opposite.

I intentionally put myself in spaces where the energy rises if I choose to be open. Outgoing. Curious. Playful.

Fashion Week became a live experiment in that work.

I talked to everyone.

Models. Photographers. Designers. Proud parents.
I “interviewed” strangers like we’d known each other for years.

And this was my favorite moment…

A mom glowing with pride as her daughter walked her first NYFW show for @theannialouisa. 

Three generations traveled from West Virginia to witness it. They even wore the designer’s pieces themselves. Their joy lit up our entire section.

That’s the power of being in the room.

You use what you have.
You make an impression.
You talk. You laugh. You connect.

And when the frequency matches?
It locks in instantly.

Being approachable isn’t personality.
It’s a practice.

And it’s a life skill. ✨

items.caption:
The stores we listened to tonight have me in tears — stories about care, fear, language, health, and community — and what they reveal about how younger generations can support older ones.

Accounts of a health crisis, where people in her community couldn’t leave their homes. Fear is high. 

People feel they could be taken away at any time. 

So neighbors — delivery drivers, students, and friends — stepped in. 

They bring food. Supplies. Medicine. Preform Bedtime Rituals. 

Not because it was their profession — but because it was human.

Another story came from an immigrant nurse navigating multiple languages and cultures. 

Even with professional skills, speaking up in English felt intimidating. Connection was harder. 

Trust took longer. 

What made the difference wasn’t systems alone — it was individuals who helped with transportation, interpretation, registration, and follow-through. 

People who showed up consistently.

Across these stories, a pattern emerges:

support is not just financial — it is relational. 

It’s rides to appointments. 
Translation help. 
Food drop-offs. 
Technology guidance. 
Health navigation. 

And most of all — reassurance and presence.

Younger generations have tools older generations may not — mobility, digital fluency, flexible networks, and social reach. 

But the real gift isn’t technology — it’s willingness. 

Willingness to check in. 
To explain. 
To accompany. 
To advocate. 
To listen without rushing.

Intergenerational care is not charity. It’s continuity. 

Communities stay strong when experience and energy work together.

The question isn’t whether younger people can help — it’s how intentionally we choose to show up.

Sunday was full immersion. No devices. No distractions. 

Complete self-care, nervous system reset, bio-field tuning — all inside the safety of a fully shielded Faraday room.

Reiki, infrared therapies, sound beds, cymatics, AO Scan… I spent the entire day moving through modalities 

I’m just beginning to understand, but my body clearly knows what to do with. 

Last night I slept eight hours straight for the first time in probably a year. 

My mind feels clear and spacious. Emotions that have been stuck for months finally moved with tears flowing like they haven’t before. 

My brain-spin cycle slowed down just enough for some deep, dark shit to finally release.

Today I feel centered, balanced, lighter — and honestly a little overwhelmed by the potential of mastering these ancient and modern healing tools.

What I experienced:
• Traditional Reiki
• Faraday Room w/ Vogel-cut crystal light
• Infrared Chakra Rainbow Room
• Cymatic Waterbed + Sound Bowls + Seven Vibe Aura
• AO Scan (inner voice + bio-frequencies)

I’m not claiming anything other than this: it worked for me.

And I’m wildly curious where this path leads. 

Thank you to @vibeauraholisticpractice for introducing me to all this.

items.caption:
Grateful doesn’t even begin to cover it. 💛💜

@crossculturalcommunityservices 2025 fundraising committee efforts, I want to offer a deep and heartfelt thank-you. 

These gifts aren’t just financial support to the work these founders have committed to—it’s a vote of confidence in the long, intentional work of building a more equitable, accessible, and human-centered health system.

What inspires me most about CCCS is the ecosystem they’ve helped cultivate over time—one rooted in education, aging with dignity, health equity, and community-driven leadership. 

Through partnerships and grant support from organizations like Maine Health Access Foundation, Maine Initiatives @maine_initiatives , Maine Writers and Publishers Alliance @mainewriters207, CCCS has consistently shown how local action and national vision can move together.

From oral health access to aging initiatives, from capacity building to health equity education, these partners represent something powerful: a bridge between community wisdom and institutional change. 

Some operate outside federal systems, others within them—but all are aligned around a shared purpose: advancing EDI growth, strengthening education, and improving outcomes across our health systems.

As part of the fundraising committee, I’m proud to work alongside a team that doesn’t just raise funds—we map relationships, steward trust, and intentionally connect people, foundations, and public institutions into a living ecosystem of care. 

CCCS exemplifies what’s possible when values lead and collaboration follows.  We need your help!  Please reach out for volunteer opportunities.  Our fundraising committee is growing fast! 

Thank you for believing in the work. 
Thank you for investing in the people. 

And thank you for reminding us that sustainable change is built—together.

items.caption:
I’m truly honored to be surrounded by the leadership team of @crossculturalcommunityservices.  Thank you to the Host Committee, Board and all our generous sponsors. 

It has been a once in a lifetime learning experience of truly making an impact in our community. 

I’ve spent my life connecting things that weren’t designed to connect.  In tech, that means APIs — systems that speak different languages but create flow when aligned.

In community, it means people — bridging voices divided by bias or fear, helping them find shared rhythm.

At CCCS, I see that same architecture: a human interface for change.
A network of people and systems exchanging empathy, literacy, and opportunity.

When we began our fundraising work, we didn’t have all the answers — but we knew it had to start with mapping our connections.
Six months later, the results speak for themselves. 

That’s community transformation.

The real problems don’t come from bad people — they come from broken connections.

When systems don’t talk, people fall through the gaps.

But every system can be redesigned.

Every story can be rewritten — together.

Change doesn’t start with sweeping reform.
It starts small — one step, one act, one conversation.

Join us.
Stand together for change.

items.caption:
Wandering New York

Wandering the earth has its advantages. I’ve grown used to being different—it’s my default setting. In most situations, that holds true.

I can stand in a room full of strangers and say nothing—just listen. The loud ones laugh at themselves; the quiet ones don’t know where to put their hands.

There’s beauty in being unknown. In standing among a crowd and realizing how free you are. 

No limits. No rules. Just pure presence.

Right now, I’m soaking in a strange, electric energy. I don’t know why I’m here—but it’s hilarious watching people talk through most of @natashabedingfield performance.

New Yorkers are fascinating. A new breed of humanity—packed too close, moving too fast, rushing nowhere. I can’t quite match their rhythm.

A cluster of energetic energy gathered in front of me, giggling about boba. The fans around us are half-asleep, half-ecstatic. Most don’t even know the words. They mumble along anyway.

When she plays her many epic covers, only a few really sing. It feels like she’s trolling the millennial generation —dropping throwbacks for the chosen few. 

But the last song? Everyone moves. For a moment, the whole city breathes together.

items.caption:
Time in self-care and reflection has become my priority, my passion, and honestly, my favorite pastime.

Because life still gets to me.

I still get anxious. frustrated. triggered. 

I still have moments when something hits me hard enough that I can feel myself being pulled away from who I want to be.

The difference now is that I know the way back.

I’ve learned to recognize when I’m out of alignment instead of fighting the feeling or letting it carry me somewhere I don’t want to go.

I get quiet. I move. I create. I spend time outside. I reflect. 

I get curious about what I’m actually feeling and why.

And somewhere in that process, I start finding myself again.

That return has become something I deeply love.

Self-care isn’t what I do to escape my life.

It’s how I keep coming home to myself.

items.caption:
My social media isn’t really for my friends or anyone who feels my artwork is directed towards them. 

The people who know me in real life already see the circus every day. 🎪 They also know that most of my life is surprisingly mundane. 

I’m an analyst. 
I work. 
I think. 
I make things. 
I live my life.

But social media is where I’m finding me.

I’m unraveling my character. understanding how I think, how I move, what makes me feel alive, what I prioritize, and who I’m becoming.

My social media is a mirror pointed at myself.

And something interesting happens when you keep looking honestly into that mirror. 

eventually, it becomes a mirror for other people too.

That’s where the real connections happen.

Some stranger with a perfectly aligned interest, feeling, obsession, or way of seeing the world gets shuffled toward you by an algorithm neither of you really understands.

And suddenly they recognize themselves in something you made.

Maybe that’s the key.

Don’t create looking for everyone else. 

Don’t create to try to be something for someone else. 

Look for your own reflection in the mirror.

When it moves you, you’re doing it right.

📸 @kristopherkleva 
🎭 @portcitymodels

It’s where I document my experience: the wins, the failures, the friends who mentored me, the artists who inspired me, and the community who shepherd me along the ride.

I’m still learning. Still building. Still failing. Still surprising myself.

Looking back at this reel, I’m honestly blown away by how much can change when you stay curious and keep showing up.

As Kayne West once shamelessly said - “My life is dope. And I do dope shit.”

items.caption:
🎪
Years of loving people with different attachment styles have taught me one thing: reciprocal curiosity is far more valuable than labels.

TL; DR;
I’ve loved someone who was strongly dismissive avoidant. I spent years with someone who was fearful avoidant. More recently, I’ve experienced a relationship with someone who leaned more anxious.

I’m an extremely curious person, so navigating these dynamics has become a lifelong research project, one I’m not sure I’ll ever master.

Ironically, those relationships helped me realize something about myself. I feel fundamentally secure. 

Not because I never get anxious or always know the right thing to say.

Typically, the opposite but because I’ve learned to recognize my own reflections in the people I have fallen in love with.

What I’ve learned is that attachment theory isn’t about labeling people. It’s about becoming curious.

To me, emotional intelligence is understanding yourself without abandoning yourself, while creating enough safety for someone else to do the same.

Note to my future self:

When you meet someone, learn what closeness means to them. Learn what makes them feel safe. Learn what makes them withdraw.

Not to manage them, but so you can understand them.

At the same time, don’t lose yourself trying to earn someone’s love. If someone isn’t curious about what hurts you, pay attention to their actions.

Do they ask how you feel?

Do they communicate their boundaries?

Can you stay emotionally regulated together when conversations become difficult?

Do you feel warm? Invited? Safe enough to be your authentic self?

Or do you feel like you’re constantly trying to be chosen?

If it isn’t aligned, it doesn’t have to become complicated. Keep it simple. Stay curious. Let trust develop at a pace that feels safe for both of you.

Say the words out loud. Be authentic. Trust that your authentic self is worthy of being loved exactly as it is.

Love people where they’re at, but don’t abandon where you are while you’re doing it.

items.caption:
🎪

People see the 30 seconds on the runway and must think “what an easy gig”. 

The whole experience culminates in a single photo sometimes. 

People don’t see the early mornings. The workouts. The stretching. The self-doubt. The practice. The thousands of tiny decisions made long before the lights come on.

The work happens at during everyday life.

It happens in front of mirrors. It happens in the gym. It happens in the quiet moments when you’re learning to carry yourself with a little more intention, a little more presence, a little more poise.

A runway walk may only last a minute, but it asks you to bring your whole self with you.

Then there’s backstage.

The wonderfully chaotic part.

The laughter. The last-minute adjustments. The encouragement. The shared nervous energy. The collective transformation that happens as everyone prepares to step into the spotlight.

We all feel that.  And it feels amazing!!

As a dude, I’ll admit I have it relatively easy. 

I show up, look hot, try not to ruin my hair, put on the kit, and remember where I’m supposed to do with my hands.

Meanwhile, I’m surrounded by artists performing miracles with fabric, makeup, styling, accessories, and pure creative force.

The 2026 @maine_crafts_association Stitch Runway Show did not disappoint.

To all my backstage fashion friends: thank you for the laughs, the energy, and the reminder that some of the best parts of show happen long before anyone sees the runway.

Represented by @portcitymodels

items.caption:
As a maker, I didn’t expect to fall for runway.

I’m wired for systems, details, iteration — for noticing how tiny adjustments change the entire experience of a thing.

Turns out… runway speaks that language fluently.

The walk.
The carriage of the shoulders.
The architecture of a pose.
The strange engineering of confidence, timing, tension, release.

What surprised me most about the 2026 Makers Way Runway Show wasn’t the fashion.

It was discovering a local community that approaches presence the way makers approach craft — through experimentation, observation, play, repetition, and an almost irrational devotion to nuance.

Practicing with friends.
Geeking out over movement.
Refining the nearly invisible details most people would never notice.

Some may call it performative.

Maybe.

But so is music. 🎼
So is dance.💃 
So is design. 💻

So is every art form that asks us to intentionally shape how an experience is felt.

Runway, I’ve learned, is not just something you do.

It’s something you build.

Runway is a Makers Way.

Extra special thanks to @aquariusfunkk for helping me shape my runway approach.

Represented by @portcitymodels

items.caption:
Back then, I remember when all of my creativity revolved around being behind the camera… or behind the FPV goggles.

Videographer for hire.
Editor for sale.
Drone captain in charge.

Those were fun chapters. I found community through a very specific skill set — a unique way to contribute, create, and belong.

These days, though, I feel like I owe it to myself to build my creativity around being… and looking inward.

Don’t get me wrong — it’s still wicked fun to cut together a video, find the perfect song, and make something hit just right.

But nowadays… I feel like I’m the music video.

And I guess that’s OK.

items.caption:
For most of my life I thought about the body in terms of muscles, emotions, or stress.

But underneath all of that we’re electrical systems.

Every cell runs on voltage.
Every emotion has a frequency.
Change the input → the system changes.

What people call “chakras,” I’m approaching as seven energy nodes in a closed electrical circuit. More functional than mystical.

So before I started working with them, I ran an AO scan — basically a frequency assessment that shows where my system is overcharged, undercharged, or out of resonance.

This became my baseline.

From here, the experiment begins:
→  identify missing frequencies
→  counteract through light, sound, color, voice, & environment
→  observe how behavior outputs change
→  repeat daily

Some days I need confidence.
Some days I need grounding.
Some days I need expression.
Every day is different.

This is Part Zero. The diagnostic.
Next up: Part One — the Root.

Follow along if you’re curious how this unfolds.

Inverted stability work (pike push-ups + vibration plates) continues to be the real cheat code. 

It forces everything to organize while upside down.

The trick is just the celebration. The preparation is the transformation.

items.caption:
Why I wander before dawn. 

Most people only experience certain spaces at peak volume — packed with bodies, noise, urgency, and expectation. 

I love those moments too, but my secret joy has always happened in the hours before all of that arrives.

Early mornings in places built for thousands feel almost sacred. 

Without the crowds, I get to witness the architecture, the light, the echoes, the quiet logic of how a place is designed to serve human life. 

You can’t notice any of that when the space is doing its job at full capacity.

Having it to myself gives me room to reflect, to show gratitude, and to pause inside a world that rarely slows down on its own. 

It’s where I reorganize my thoughts, check in with my values, and remember what matters to me before the day starts making demands.

It’s a small ritual — one I hope to never stop doing — and honestly it’s been one of the greatest blessings I’ve been given. 

The world feels chaotic, but these quiet moments remind me I still get to choose how I enter it.

items.caption:
One of the most romantic things you can do is live long enough to love someone for the full arc.

Nobody talks about longevity inside relationships. 

We talk about chemistry, timing, values, sex, aesthetics — but the quiet question underneath is:

Can we make it long enough to enjoy the whole thing?

As we get older we start thinking about care, decline, and logistics. We watch parents lose mobility, lose memory, lose dignity, and we realize how physical partnership really is.

You don’t have to be a “hottie,” but longevity requires honoring your body together. 

Muscle mass, VO₂ max, metabolic health, and social bonds are all survival variables after 60.

Harvard’s 85-year study found that relationships were the strongest predictor of healthy aging. 

Gerontologists call it health concordance — couples literally age in parallel.

If I want to love you until 70+ years old, I need this body to serve, carry, play, hold, and remember.

I want to live long so I can love long.

How long do you want to go?

#longevity #healthspan #relationships #agingwell fitat50

It’s the weight on the bar.
It’s how the muscle grows.

There’s a reason I keep coming back to the work of Angela Duckworth and her book Grit—because the science is clear:
resilience is trainable.

If this season feels heavy—
your job,
your family,
your heart,
or just the moon pulling things loose—

this is your reminder:
You don’t rebuild by waiting.
You rebuild by showing up again.

2026 isn’t about becoming someone else.
It’s about becoming stronger at being you.

Keep going.
Even when it’s awkward.
Especially when it’s hard.

#Grit #Resilience #FailForward #TrainTheMind #DoItAgain

items.caption:
I’ve been sitting with something lately.

In relational therapy, they talk about rupture and repair — the idea that it’s not the absence of failure that builds trust, intimacy, or growth… it’s what we do after we fall on our face.

Angela Duckworth calls it GRIT: passion + perseverance over time. Not perfection. Not talent. Time in the arena. Time eating a little dirt.

Failure isn’t a verdict.
It’s feedback.
It’s information.
It’s the place where we finally stop performing and start becoming.

When things fall apart, there’s always a fifty percent we bring to the table. 

That’s not blame — that’s power. That’s agency. That’s where growth lives.

And here’s the part we don’t talk about enough — FAILURE can actually bring JOY.

Not because it feels good in the moment — but because it carries anticipation.

Anticipation that you’re learning.
Anticipation that you’re getting closer.
Anticipation that this version of you won’t be the final release.

So fail fast.
Fail honestly.
Fail with curiosity instead of shame.

Then repair.
Refactor.

And release the next iteration of yourself — a little more grounded, a little more resilient, a little more you.

I’m rooting for you. Always.

items.caption:
Yesterday I talked about how underestimating people is the fastest way to fumble opportunities.

But here’s the twist I had to face myself…
the person I was underestimating the most was me.

All those little thoughts —
“I don’t look like them.”
“I don’t dress like them.”
“My life isn’t polished enough.”
That’s not humility.
That’s self-sabotage dressed up as realism.

If you said those things to someone else, they’d walk away.

So why speak to yourself like that?

This version of me is choosing to level up.

Choosing to believe I belong in the rooms I walk into.

Choosing to stop treating myself like the weakest character in my own video game.

Never underestimate the people around you.

But most importantly — never underestimate yourself.

Let’s embrace failure and transform one version at a time.

items.caption:
Someone recently asked me if I just started making videos.  About me.  Yes! 

However I’ve edited thousands of hours of footage including building a full blown video content management production engine. 

Not too long ago, I made a commitment to be the main character in my art after losing my passion by seeking approval from someone ungrateful for my talent or time.  Since then my creativity has EXPLODED 💥

I’ve been editing videos for 32 years as a passion and art therapy. I thought i had lost this award in a messy decoupling.  Today, it was magically returned to my doorstep. 

It was the sign I was looking for and I think I’m ready to collaborate with others again. 

HMU and let’s make something fun. 🎥🎬🍿📼

items.caption:
I’m building a Personal Health Operating System that goes beyond weight loss and focuses on performance, recovery, and longevity.

 I’ve recomposed my body by dropping fat while preserving muscle and metabolism, and now I’m training for capability—strength, balance, and skill—supported by recovery practices like sauna, red light, and sleep. 

Habit stacking makes the whole system sustainable, so the goal isn’t just to look better, but to function better and age stronger. What looks like “weight loss” is actually recomposition: I burned fat, kept muscle, and preserved metabolic rate. 

My basal metabolic rate is still 2,463 calories a day because lean tissue drives metabolism, not the number on the scale.

The interesting part is how it happened. I stacked a set of small rituals — F45 strength training, sauna, red light therapy, breathwork, flexibility training, and now handstand work.

These aren’t random wellness trends; they generate specific biological signals that increase mitochondrial density, improve tissue recovery, activate brown fat, and train the nervous system to comply instead of resist.

The segmental data from InBody shows I’m disproportionately strong in my arms, legs, and trunk relative to population averages — which means my body is structurally ready to support more advanced skills like handstands. 

At 48 years old, I’m more muscular, more symmetric, and carrying less fat than I was a decade ago.

This year isn’t about looking better — it’s about engineering a body that can do harder things, for longer, with better recovery.

 A generation that many don’t understand, yet their rhythm hits deeper than words can explain.

items.caption:
Wandering the earth has its advantages. I’ve grown used to being different—it’s my default setting. In most situations, that holds true.  I can stand in a room full of strangers and say nothing—just listen. The loud ones laugh at themselves; the quiet ones don’t know where to put their hands.

There’s beauty in being unknown. In standing among a crowd and realizing how free you are. No limits. No rules. Just pure presence.

 New Yorkers are fascinating. A new breed of humanity—packed too close, moving too fast, rushing nowhere. I can’t quite match their rhythm.

A cluster of energy  gathered in front of me, giggling about boba. The fans around us are half-asleep, half-ecstatic. Most don’t even know the words. They mumble along anyway.

When Natasha plays many of her epic covers ,only a few really sing. It feels like she’s trolling us—dropping throwbacks for the chosen few. 

But the last song? “Unwritten” Everyone moves.

For a moment, the whole city breathes together
